entries.answer: Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy; oxygenic photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water and releases oxygen.
A cell is the basic structural and functional unit of living organisms.
DNA stores hereditary genetic information in living organisms and some viruses.
RNA is a nucleic acid involved in information transfer, gene regulation and sometimes catalysis.
Proteins are biological polymers made from amino acids that perform structural, catalytic, transport and signaling functions.
Biological evolution is change in heritable characteristics of populations across generations.
Natural selection is a process in which heritable differences affect reproductive success, changing trait frequencies across generations.
A virus is an infectious biological entity that replicates using a host cell's molecular machinery.
Mitochondria are organelles involved in cellular energy metabolism and ATP production.
A ribosome is a molecular machine that synthesizes proteins from messenger RNA.
A chromosome is a DNA-containing structure that carries genetic information.
A gene is a region of genetic material associated with functional products or regulation.
A genome is the complete genetic material of an organism or virus.
Bacteria are diverse single-celled organisms without a membrane-bound nucleus.
Fungi are organisms belonging to a distinct biological kingdom and include yeasts, molds and mushrooms.
Ecology studies interactions among organisms and between organisms and their environment.
An ecosystem includes living organisms and their physical environment interacting as a system.
A food chain describes the transfer of energy and matter through feeding relationships.
